input_findings_summary: 12 findings from the third independent pass (fresh, clean-context, iteration 4): 2 CRITICAL, 6 WARNING, 4 SUGGESTION. This pass spent the last of the gate's 3-pass budget.
pushback_verification: All 12 verified against the tree before any edit; zero stale. Confirmed independently rather than relayed: the self-reference rule is named by no task except 4.2's authoring guidance, and is the only one of 21 scenarios with no implementing or testing task (finding 1); the baseline's wording really is 'The engine reads ONLY … rulings … engine-opaque', subject THE ENGINE (finding 2); CLAUDE.md:113 really does carry a present-tense 'eighteen small stages' for the active program and :145 a present-tense schema version, against a live stage count of 18 (finding 8); orbit/specs/ holds 20 capability directories today, so this change's own archive moves it (finding 6); docs/cli.md's JSON example really is fabricated against validate.ts's actual output (finding 11); orbit-audit-drift Category 3(b) really does claim counts and version pins (finding 9). One abort fired during application — a design.md anchor did not match and the all-or-nothing guard wrote NOTHING rather than a partial edit set, which is the intended behaviour of the verify-every-anchor-first discipline adopted earlier in this program.

resolutions.title: The self-reference rule is normative and scenario-backed, but no input is declared for it and no task implements or tests it
resolutions.action: RATIFIED OPTION B (chat, 'walk them' against a stated lean). The rule is DEMOTED from a SHALL to an authoring RECORD and its scenario deleted (21 scenarios, none now taskless). The spec states the hazard concretely and then states why it is not a check: detecting it needs the per-source input region, an input nowhere declared and one R-crc-10 forbids leaving unnamed — 'the one place in this capability where judgment slipped back into a check'. Enforcement moves to where it can actually live: task 4.2's authoring instruction. This restores the design's opening R-crc-10 claim, which the rule had quietly falsified.

resolutions.title: `byType.sources`'s item unit is undefined, and contributing to `summary.totals` breaks the existing `totals.items === items.length` invariant
resolutions.action: Named the item unit: ONE ITEM IS ONE DECLARED SOURCE, `failed` = sources with at least one finding, and a registry-level fault counts as one failed pseudo-item so a non-zero exit can never sit beside zero failed items. Also settled the invariant question the finding raised rather than leaving it to be discovered: source items do NOT enter `items[]`, so `summary.totals.items === items.length` no longer holds on a registry-bearing run — retired DELIBERATELY, stated in both design D5b and task 3.2, and covered by a test, because a consumer cross-checking the two would otherwise break silently.

resolutions.title: The overlap with `orbit-audit-drift` Category 3(b) is unacknowledged
resolutions.action: Named the overlap in the design rather than leaving it implicit: `orbit-audit-drift` Category 3 already extracts quantitative claims (counts, version pins) from governing docs and raises a CRITICAL on disagreement — Case 1 records that this is how the schema-version defect was caught. Stated why two surfaces on one figure is acceptable here and is NOT the 'two capabilities in charge of one rule' defect the proposal rejects elsewhere: different mechanisms with different reliability, and audit-drift covers exactly the unmarked figures the lint declares it can never see. Noted the possible later refinement (audit-drift suppressing claims inside marked spans) as an out-of-scope MODIFIED delta.

resolutions.title: The ruling-entry grammar — the one genuinely new parse — is prose, where the change's other two grammars are decision tables
resolutions.action: Closed both loose terms in the spec: TOP-LEVEL is a list item whose marker begins at indent 0-3 (CommonMark's allowance) and is not nested inside another list item; the SECTION runs from the `## Rulings index` heading to the next heading at `##` or higher. Recorded the reason for defining them — the live doc satisfies either reading, so the ambiguity would have shipped unexposed — and added the negative fixture the finding asked for to task 1.1: a nested bullet whose bold span matches the prefix, which must not count.

final_assessment: All 12 resolved: 9 obvious-fix, 3 decision-lane with chat ratification. The headline is a REVERSAL: finding 2 overturned the option-B ruling made two walks ago on my recommendation, and the change now carries a MODIFIED delta for orbit-architecture-engine with all six baseline scenarios preserved verbatim plus one new, and a stamped base fingerprint. Finding 1 went the other way — the self-reference rule I authored in response to the external pass is DEMOTED from a check to a record, because its input was never declared and R-crc-10 forbids exactly that. Capabilities 1 → 2 and tasks 18 → 19: both inside R-crc-1's ceiling, but 19 of a <20 budget is the tightest this change has been.
